metadata.title: Phase transition of the largest eigenvalue for non-null complex sample covariance matrices
metadata.authors: Jinho Baik, Gérard Ben Arous, Sandrine Péché

nodes.name: Sample covariance matrix
nodes.statement: Given $M$ i.i.d. complex Gaussian samples $\vec{y}_1,\dots,\vec{y}_M$ each $N\times 1$ with covariance $\Sigma$, the centered sample matrix is $X=[\vec{y}_1-\overline{Y},\dots,\vec{y}_M-\overline{Y}]$ and $S=\frac1N XX^*$ is the sample covariance matrix; $\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_N>0$ are the sample eigenvalues, $\ell_1,\dots,\ell_N$ the population eigenvalues.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines the sample covariance matrix S = (1/N) X X* and its eigenvalues for complex Gaussian samples.

nodes.name: Airy kernel
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{A}(u,v) = \frac{Ai(u)Ai'(v)-Ai'(u)Ai(v)}{u-v}$, with $\mathbf{A}_x$ the operator on $L^2((x,\infty))$ with this kernel; equivalently $\mathbf{A}(u,v)=\int_0^\infty Ai(u+z)Ai(z+v)\,dz$.

nodes.name: Functions $s^{(m)}, t^{(m)}$
nodes.statement: $s^{(m)}(u)=\frac1{2\pi}\int e^{iua+i a^3/3}\frac1{(ia)^m}\,da$ (contour from $\infty e^{5i\pi/6}$ to $\infty e^{i\pi/6}$ with $a=0$ above) and $t^{(m)}(v)=\frac1{2\pi}\int e^{iva+i a^3/3}(-ia)^{m-1}\,da$. Equivalently $t^{(m)}(v)=(-d/dv)^{m-1} Ai(v)$.

nodes.name: Distribution functions $F_k(x)$
nodes.statement: $F_k(x)=\det(1-\mathbf{A}_x)\cdot \det\bigl(\delta_{mn}-\langle (1-\mathbf{A}_x)^{-1} s^{(m)}, t^{(n)}\rangle\bigr)_{1\le m,n\le k}$, with $F_0(x)=\det(1-\mathbf{A}_x)=F_{GUE}(x)$.

nodes.name: Finite GUE distributions $G_k(x)$
nodes.statement: $G_k(x)=\frac1{Z_k}\int_{-\infty}^x\!\!\cdots\!\!\int_{-\infty}^x \prod_{i<j}|\xi_i-\xi_j|^2 \prod_{i=1}^k e^{-\xi_i^2/2}\,d\xi_1\cdots d\xi_k$, the distribution of the largest eigenvalue of $k\times k$ GUE.

nodes.name: Interpolating distributions $F_k(x;w_1,\dots,w_k)$
nodes.statement: $F_k(x;w_1,\dots,w_k)=\det(1-\mathbf{A}_x)\cdot\det\bigl(1-\langle (1-\mathbf{A}_x)^{-1} s^{(m)}(w_1,\dots,w_m), t^{(n)}(w_1,\dots,w_{n-1})\rangle\bigr)_{1\le m,n\le k}$ with parameter-dependent $s^{(m)}, t^{(m)}$.

nodes.name: Last passage time $L(N,M)$
nodes.statement: For independent $X(i,j)$ on $\{1,\dots,N\}\times\{1,\dots,M\}$, $L(N,M)=\max_{\pi\in (1,1)\nearrow(N,M)}\sum_{(i,j)\in\pi}X(i,j)$, the maximum over up/right paths from $(1,1)$ to $(N,M)$.

nodes.name: Tracy-Widom GUE limit (cited)
nodes.statement: When $\Sigma=I$ and $M,N\to\infty$ with $M/N\to\gamma^2\ge 1$: $\mathbb{P}\bigl((\lambda_1-((1+\gamma)/\gamma)^2)\cdot \gamma M^{2/3}/(1+\gamma)^{4/3}\le x\bigr)\to F_{GUE}(x)$.
conclusions: Largest sample eigenvalue $\lambda_1$, suitably scaled, converges to GUE Tracy-Widom distribution $F_{GUE}$

nodes.name: Péché's earlier result (cited)
nodes.statement: If $\ell_{r+1}=\dots=\ell_N=1$ and $\ell_1=\dots=\ell_r<2$ are fixed, then as $M=N\to\infty$, $\mathbb{P}((\lambda_1-4)\cdot 2^{-4/3}M^{2/3}\le x)\to F_{GUE}(x)$.
conclusions: Same Tracy-Widom GUE limit holds when distinguished population eigenvalues are sub-critical ($<2$)

nodes.name: Main theorem: phase transition for largest eigenvalue
nodes.statement: Let $\ell_{r+1}=\dots=\ell_N=1$. (a) If $\ell_1=\dots=\ell_k=1+\gamma^{-1}$ and $\ell_{k+1},\dots,\ell_r$ in compact $(0,1+\gamma^{-1})$, then $\mathbb{P}((\lambda_1-(1+\gamma^{-1})^2)\frac{\gamma}{(1+\gamma)^{4/3}}M^{2/3}\le x)\to F_k(x)$. (b) If $\ell_1=\cdots=\ell_k$ in compact $(1+\gamma^{-1},\infty)$ and $\ell_{k+1},\dots,\ell_r$ in compact $(0,\ell_1)$, then $\mathbb{P}((\lambda_1-(\ell_1+\frac{\ell_1\gamma^{-2}}{\ell_1-1}))\frac{\sqrt{M}}{\sqrt{\ell_1^2-\ell_1^2\gamma^{-2}/(\ell_1-1)^2}}\le x)\to G_k(x)$.
assumptions: $M,N\to\infty$ with $M/N=\gamma^2$ in a compact subset of $[1,\infty)$
conclusions: (a) sub-critical / critical regime: scaled $\lambda_1$ converges to new distribution $F_k$ at rate $M^{2/3}$
(b) super-critical regime: scaled $\lambda_1$ converges to $G_k$ at Gaussian rate $\sqrt{M}$
Critical value $1+\gamma^{-1}$ separates the two phases

nodes.name: Convergence in probability of $\lambda_1$
nodes.statement: Under same assumptions: (a) if $\ell_1=\dots=\ell_k=1+\gamma^{-1}$, then $\lambda_1\to (1+\gamma^{-1})^2$ in probability. (b) if $\ell_1=\dots=\ell_k>1+\gamma^{-1}$, then $\lambda_1\to \ell_1(1+\frac{\gamma^{-2}}{\ell_1-1})$ in probability.
conclusions: $\lambda_1$ converges in probability to $(1+\gamma^{-1})^2$ in case (a)
$\lambda_1$ converges in probability to $\ell_1(1+\gamma^{-2}/(\ell_1-1))$ in case (b)

nodes.name: Finite-dimensional sample limit
nodes.statement: If $N=k$ fixed and $\ell_1=\cdots=\ell_k$, then as $M\to\infty$, $\mathbb{P}((\lambda_1-\ell_1)\frac{\sqrt{M}}{\ell_1}\le x)\to G_k(x)$ and $\lambda_1\to \ell_1$ in probability.
conclusions: Properly scaled $\lambda_1$ converges to $G_k(x)$
$\lambda_1\to\ell_1$ in probability

nodes.name: Real-sample analogue of main theorem
nodes.statement: For real sample covariance, Theorem 1.4 still holds true for different limiting distributions but with the same scaling; the critical value of distinguished eigenvalues is again expected to be $1+\gamma^{-1}$.
conclusions: Same scaling and same critical value $1+\gamma^{-1}$ expected for real samples

nodes.name: Interpolating distributions at the critical scaling
nodes.statement: If $\ell_{r+1}=\dots=\ell_N=1$ and $\ell_j=1+\gamma^{-1}-\frac{(1+\gamma)^{2/3}w_j}{\gamma M^{1/3}}$ for $1\le j\le k$, then $\mathbb{P}((\lambda_1-(1+\gamma^{-1})^2)\frac{\gamma}{(1+\gamma)^{4/3}}M^{2/3}\le x)\to F_k(x;w_1,\dots,w_k)$.
assumptions: $w_j$ in a compact subset of $\mathbb{R}$, other $\ell_j$ in compact $(0, 1+\gamma^{-1})$
conclusions: Scaled $\lambda_1$ converges to interpolating distribution $F_k(x;w_1,\dots,w_k)$

nodes.name: Fredholm-determinant formula for $\mathbb{P}(\lambda_1\le \xi)$
nodes.statement: For $0<q<\min\{\pi_j\}$, the kernel $\mathbf{K}_{M,N}(\eta,\zeta)=\frac{M}{(2\pi i)^2}\int_\Gamma\!\!\int_\Sigma e^{-\eta M(z-q)+\zeta M(w-q)}\frac1{w-z}(z/w)^M\prod_k\frac{\pi_k-w}{\pi_k-z}\,dz\,dw$ defines a trace-class operator on $L^2((\xi,\infty))$ with $\mathbb{P}(\lambda_1\le\xi)=\det(1-\mathbf{K}_{M,N}|_{(\xi,\infty)})$.
assumptions: $\Gamma$ encloses $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_N$ in $\{\Re z>q\}$, $\Sigma$ encloses $0$ in $\{\Re w<q\}$, both counter-clockwise
conclusions: $\mathbb{P}(\lambda_1\le\xi)$ equals the Fredholm determinant of $1-\mathbf{K}_{M,N}$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.1 (Fredholm formula)
nodes.statement: Start from the eigenvalue density (assuming distinct $\pi_j$), apply Andreief's identity, write the kernel via Hankel's contour integral for $1/\Gamma(a)$, use Cramer's rule, and identify $CA^{-1}B$ as the kernel; extend by l'Hopital when $\pi_j$'s coincide.

nodes.name: Reduce to determinantal integral
nodes.statement: Use $V(\lambda)=\det(\lambda_k^{j-1})$ and the symmetry of the density to write $\mathbb{P}(\lambda_1\le\xi)$ as a multiple integral of two determinants times $(1-\chi_{(\xi,\infty)})$ factors.

nodes.name: Apply Andreief's identity
nodes.statement: Use $\int\cdots\int \det(f_j(x_k))\det(g_j(x_k))\prod d\mu(x_k)=\det(\int f_j g_k\,d\mu)$ to collapse the integral to a single determinant of pairwise integrals.

nodes.name: Introduce $\phi_j,\Phi_k,A,B,C$ and apply $\det(A-BP_\xi C)$
nodes.statement: Set $\phi_j(\lambda)=\lambda^{j-1+\nu}e^{-Mq\lambda}$, $\Phi_k(\lambda)=e^{-M(\pi_k-q)\lambda}$, $A_{jk}=\int \phi_j\Phi_k$ (Gamma matrix), $B,C$ the natural operators, $P_\xi$ projector to $(\xi,\infty)$; obtain $\mathbb{P}(\lambda_1\le\xi)=C''\det(1-P_\xi CA^{-1}B P_\xi)$ with $C''=1$.

nodes.name: Compute $A^{-1}B$ via Cramer's rule and Hankel integral
nodes.statement: Use Cramer's rule and Hankel's contour formula $\frac1{2\pi i}\int_\Sigma e^w/w^a\,dw=1/\Gamma(a)$ to write $(A^{-1}B)(j,\zeta)$ as a contour integral involving the products $\prod_{k\ne j}(w-\pi_k)/(\pi_j-\pi_k)$.

nodes.name: Combine over $j$ via residue identity
nodes.statement: Sum over $j$ using the $\Gamma$-contour identity $\frac1{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma z^M e^{-\eta Mz}\frac1{w-z}\prod\frac{w-\pi_k}{z-\pi_k}\,dz=\sum_j\pi_j^M e^{-M\pi_j\eta}\prod_{k\ne j}(w-\pi_k)/(\pi_j-\pi_k)$ to obtain the announced double-contour formula for $\mathbf{K}_{M,N}$.

nodes.name: Extend to coinciding $\pi_j$ by limit
nodes.statement: Take limits via l'Hospital when some $\pi_j$'s coincide, completing the identity.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue density of complex Gaussian sample covariance
nodes.statement: $p(\lambda)=\frac1C \frac{\det(e^{-M\pi_j\lambda_k})_{1\le j,k\le N}}{V(\pi)}V(\lambda)\prod_{j=1}^N \lambda_j^{M-N}$, obtained from the Wishart density and the Harish-Chandra-Itzykson-Zuber integral over $U(N)$.

nodes.name: Operator-product form $\mathbf{K}_{M,N}=\int \mathbf{H}\,\mathbf{J}$
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{K}_{M,N}(\eta,\zeta)=\int_0^\infty \mathbf{H}(\eta+y)\mathbf{J}(\zeta+y)\,dy$ where $\mathbf{H},\mathbf{J}$ are single contour integrals; this writes the kernel as a Hilbert-Schmidt product, enabling steepest-descent analysis.

nodes.name: Convergence of $\mathcal{H},\mathcal{J}$ at the Airy point
nodes.statement: With $\alpha=2/3$, $\mu=((1+\gamma)/\gamma)^2$, $\nu=(1+\gamma)^{4/3}/\gamma$, $q=p_c-\epsilon/(\nu M^{1/3})$ and $p_c=\gamma/(\gamma+1)$: there exist $C,c,M_0>0$ s.t. $|Z_M\mathcal{H}(u)-\mathcal{H}_\infty(u)|\le Ce^{-cu}/M^{1/3}$ for $u\ge U$ and $|Z_M^{-1}\mathcal{J}(v)-\mathcal{J}_\infty(v)|\le Ce^{-cv}/M^{1/3}$ for $v\ge V$, $M\ge M_0$, uniformly for $\gamma$ in a compact subset of $[1,\infty)$.
assumptions: $0\le k\le r$ with $\pi_1^{-1}=\dots=\pi_k^{-1}=1+\gamma^{-1}$, others in compact $(0,1+\gamma^{-1})$
conclusions: Hilbert-Schmidt-type estimates between $Z_M\mathcal{H}$ and $\mathcal{H}_\infty$
Hilbert-Schmidt-type estimates between $Z_M^{-1}\mathcal{J}$ and $\mathcal{J}_\infty$

nodes.name: Steep-descent of $\Re f$ on $\Gamma_1\cup\Gamma_2$
nodes.statement: For $\gamma\ge 1$, $\Re(f(z))$ is decreasing for $z\in\Gamma_1\cup\Gamma_2$ as $\Re(z)$ increases; moreover $R$ can be chosen so that $\max_{z\in\Gamma_3}\Re f(z)\le \Re f(p_*)$, where $p_*=p_c+2(1-p_c)e^{i\pi/3}$.
conclusions: $\Gamma$ is a steep-descent curve for $f$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: Compute $F_1'(t),F_2'(x),F_3(y)$ explicitly on each piece; bound the polynomial $T_1(t)=(\gamma+1)^2 t^2-(\gamma^2-1)t+2\gamma\ge 2$ to show monotonicity; argue $F_3(y)$ can be made arbitrarily small by taking $R$ large.

nodes.name: Steep-descent of $\Re(-f)$ on $\Sigma_1\cup\Sigma_2$
nodes.statement: For $\gamma\ge 1$, $\Re(-f(z))$ is decreasing on $\Sigma_1\cup\Sigma_2$ as $\Re(z)$ decreases; and $R$ can be chosen so that $\max_{z\in\Sigma_3}\Re(-f(z))\le \Re(-f(p_*))$, with $p_*=p_c+2p_c e^{2i\pi/3}$.
conclusions: $\Sigma$ is a steep-descent curve for $-f$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: Same scheme as Lemma 3.1: explicit derivatives on each $\Sigma_j$ and a polynomial positivity check for $T_2(x)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1 (Airy regime convergence)
nodes.statement: Split $\Gamma=\Gamma'\cup\Gamma''$ near and far from $p_c$; use Lemma 3.1 to bound $|Z_M\mathcal{H}''(u)|$ exponentially small in $M$; use Taylor's theorem for $f$ to bound $|Z_M\mathcal{H}'(u)-\mathcal{H}_\infty'(u)|=O(M^{-1/3})$; treat $u$ in a compact set and $u>0$ separately. Same scheme for $\mathcal{J}$ via Lemma 3.2.

nodes.name: Choose contours and split $\Gamma=\Gamma'\cup\Gamma''$
nodes.statement: Define $\Gamma=\Gamma_0\cup\Gamma_1\cup\Gamma_2\cup\Gamma_3$ and split into local part $\Gamma'$ inside $|z-p_c|<\delta$ and far part $\Gamma''$; correspondingly split $\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}'+\mathcal{H}''$.

nodes.name: Far-part bound via Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: Use Lemma 3.1 ($\max_{\Gamma''}\Re f\le f(p_c)-\nu^3\delta^3/6$) to obtain $|Z_M\mathcal{H}''(u)|\le e^{-\nu^3\delta^3 M/12}$ for large $M$.

nodes.name: Local Taylor expansion bound
nodes.statement: By Taylor's theorem, $|f(z)-f(p_c)-\frac{f^{(3)}(p_c)}{6}(z-p_c)^3|\le C_0|z-p_c|^4\le \frac{\nu^3}{6}|z-p_c|^3$, allowing replacement of $f$ by its cubic on $\Gamma'$.

nodes.name: Compare $\mathcal{H}'$ and $\mathcal{H}_\infty'$
nodes.statement: Sub-split $\Gamma'=\Gamma_1'\cup\Gamma_2'$; on each piece estimate $|e^{M(f(z)-f(p_c))}-e^{M\nu^3(z-p_c)^3/3}|$ and $|g(p_c)/g(z)-1|$ to obtain $|Z_M\mathcal{H}'-\mathcal{H}_\infty'|\le C/M^{1/3}$.

nodes.name: Symmetric treatment of $\mathcal{J}$
nodes.statement: Repeat the splitting argument on contour $\Sigma$ using Lemma 3.2; obtain $|Z_M^{-1}\mathcal{J}-\mathcal{J}_\infty|\le C/M^{1/3}$; treat $v$ in compact set and $v>0$ separately.

nodes.name: Combine into Hilbert-Schmidt convergence
nodes.statement: Combine local and far-part estimates to obtain the trace-class convergence of $\mathcal{K}_{M,N}\to\mathcal{K}_\infty$ from which the Fredholm determinants converge.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.4 (a)
nodes.statement: From Proposition 3.1, $\mathbb{P}((\lambda_1-(1+\gamma^{-1})^2)\frac{\gamma}{(1+\gamma)^{4/3}}M^{2/3}\le x)\to \det(1-K_\infty)$ where $K_\infty(u,v)=\int_0^\infty \mathcal{H}_\infty(x+u+y)\mathcal{J}_\infty(x+v+y)\,dy$. Algebra using the Airy integral representation rewrites this as $\det(1-\mathbf{E}\mathbf{A}_x\mathbf{E}^{-1}-\sum_{m=1}^k \mathbf{E}s_x^{(m)}\otimes t_x^{(m)}\mathbf{E}^{-1})$, equal to $F_k(x)$.

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 3.1 to get limit kernel
nodes.statement: Use Proposition 3.1 to conclude that the kernel $\mathcal{K}_{M,N}$ converges to $K_\infty(u,v)=\int_0^\infty \mathcal{H}_\infty(x+u+y)\mathcal{J}_\infty(x+v+y)\,dy$ in trace-class on $L^2((0,\infty))$.

nodes.name: Decompose $K_\infty$ into Airy + finite-rank
nodes.statement: Using $Ai(u)=\frac{-1}{2\pi i}\int_{\Gamma_\infty}e^{-ua+a^3/3}\,da=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\Sigma_\infty}e^{ub-b^3/3}\,db$, expand $((b/a)^k-1)/(a-b)$ as $\sum_{m=1}^k b^{m-1}/a^m$ to write $K_\infty=e^{-\epsilon u}\mathbf{A}_x e^{\epsilon v}+\sum_{m=1}^k e^{-\epsilon u} s^{(m)}(u)t^{(m)}(v)e^{\epsilon v}$.

nodes.name: Apply finite-rank perturbation determinant formula
nodes.statement: Apply the identity $\det(1-K-\sum a_i\otimes b_i)=\det(1-K)\det(\delta_{mn}-\langle (1-K)^{-1}a_m,b_n\rangle)$ to obtain $F_k(x)$ via Definition 1.1.

nodes.name: Well-definedness of $F_k$ and integral form of $s^{(m)}$
nodes.statement: $F_k(x)$ in Definition 1.1 is well-defined; and $s^{(m)}(u)=\sum_{\ell+3n=m-1}\frac{(-1)^n}{3^n \ell! n!}u^\ell + \frac{1}{(m-1)!}\int_\infty^u (u-y)^{m-1} Ai(y)\,dy$.
conclusions: The inner product $\langle (1-\mathbf{A}_x)^{-1} s^{(m)}, t^{(n)}\rangle$ is finite, so $F_k(x)$ is well-defined
$s^{(m)}(u)$ has the closed-form polynomial-plus-Airy-integral expression

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: Use the steepest-descent asymptotics $Ai(u)\sim e^{-2u^{3/2}/3}/(2\sqrt{\pi}u^{1/4})$ and analogous expansions for $s^{(m)},t^{(m)}$ to verify integrability of the inner product $\langle (1-\mathbf{A}_x)^{-1}s^{(m)},t^{(n)}\rangle$. The polynomial part of $s^{(m)}$ is determined by the residue at $a=0$ from the contour formula.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.6 (interpolating distributions)
nodes.statement: Identical to the proof of Theorem 1.4(a) with the new scaling $\pi_j^{-1}=1+\gamma^{-1}-w_j/M^{1/3}$; details skipped.

nodes.name: Convergence of $\mathcal{H},\mathcal{J}$ in the Gaussian regime
nodes.statement: With $\alpha=1/2$, $\mu=1/\pi_1+\gamma^{-2}/(1-\pi_1)$, $\nu=\sqrt{1/\pi_1^2-\gamma^{-2}/(1-\pi_1)^2}$, $q=\pi_1-\epsilon/(\nu\sqrt{M})$: there exist $C,c,M_0>0$ s.t. $|Z_M^{-1}\mathcal{J}(v)-\mathcal{J}_\infty(v)|\le Ce^{-cv}/\sqrt{M}$ for $v\ge V$, and $|Z_M\mathcal{H}(u)-\mathcal{H}_\infty(u)|\le Ce^{-cu}/\sqrt{M}$ for $u\ge U$.
assumptions: $\pi_1^{-1}=\dots=\pi_k^{-1}>1+\gamma^{-1}$ in compact subset of $(1+\gamma^{-1},\infty)$, others in $(0,\pi_1^{-1})$
conclusions: Quantitative pointwise/decay estimates for $\mathcal{H},\mathcal{J}$ near the Gaussian critical point $z=\pi_1$

nodes.name: Steep-descent of $-f$ on $\Sigma_1\cup\Sigma_2$ (Gaussian regime)
nodes.statement: $\Re(-f(z))$ decreases on $\Sigma_1\cup\Sigma_2$ along the prescribed orientation; for $\gamma$ in a compact subset of $[1,\infty)$, $R$ can be chosen so that $\max_{z\in\Sigma_3}\Re(-f(z))\le \Re(-f(p_*))$ with $p_*=\pi_1+2i$.
conclusions: $\Sigma$ is a steep-descent curve for $-f$ in the Gaussian regime

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: Compute $F_1'(y),F_2'(x),F_3(y)$ on each piece and use $g(s)=s/(s^2+4)$ bounds.

nodes.name: Decay of $\Re f$ on contour $\Gamma'$ in Gaussian regime
nodes.statement: There exist $\delta,c>0$ s.t. $\Re(f(z)-f(\pi_1))\le -c$ on $\Gamma_1\cup\Gamma_2$; $\Re f$ is decreasing on $\Gamma_3\cup\Gamma_4$; and $\Re(f(z)-f(\pi_1))\le \Re(f(1+i/(1+\gamma))-f(\pi_1))$ on $\Gamma_5$ for sufficiently large $R$.
conclusions: Strong decay of $\Re f$ on $\Gamma'$ ensures the integral over $\Gamma'$ is exponentially small

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement: On $\Gamma_1\cup\Gamma_2$: bound $|Re(f(x+iy)-f(x))|\le C_1|y|$ and use real-axis monotonicity of $\Re f$ between the two critical points $\pi_1$ and $1/(\mu\pi_1)$. On $\Gamma_3$: parameterize and show $G(t)$ is decreasing via $G'(-1)\le 0$. On $\Gamma_4$: $F_4'(x)\le 0$ since $\mu\ge ((1+\gamma)/\gamma)^2\ge 1$. On $\Gamma_5$: take $R$ large.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.1 (Gaussian regime convergence)
nodes.statement: For (i): construct steep-descent contour $\Sigma$ for $-f$, split $\Sigma=\Sigma'\cup\Sigma''$ near and far from $\pi_1$, use Lemma 4.1 plus Taylor's theorem to bound errors. For (ii): Cauchy's residue theorem extracts the residue at $z=\pi_1$ and writes $Z_M\mathcal{H}(u)=\mathcal{H}_1(u)+I(\Gamma')$. Show $\mathcal{H}_1(u)\to\mathcal{H}_\infty(u)$ via Taylor expansion in $a/\sqrt{M}$, and $I(\Gamma')$ is exponentially small via Lemma 4.2.

nodes.name: Set up Gaussian-regime contours $\Sigma,\Gamma'$
nodes.statement: Define $\Sigma=\bigcup\Sigma_j$ near $\pi_1$ and $\Gamma'=\bigcup\Gamma_j$ enclosing all zeros of $g$ except $\pi_1$, both made steep-descent for $-f$ and $f$ respectively.

nodes.name: Residue extraction at $z=\pi_1$
nodes.statement: Apply Cauchy's residue theorem to write $\mathcal{H}(u)=i\nu\sqrt{M}\,\mathrm{Res}_{z=\pi_1}(\cdots) + (\nu\sqrt{M}/2\pi)\int_{\Gamma'}(\cdots)\,dz$, isolating the dominant residue contribution.

nodes.name: Local expansion of residue term $\mathcal{H}_1$
nodes.statement:
Set $z=\pi_1+a/(
u\sqrt{M})$; expand $\exp(M(f(\pi_1+a/(
u\sqrt{M}))-f(\pi_1)))$ as $e^{-a^2/2}(1+O(1/\sqrt{M}))$ and $g(\pi_1)/g(\pi_1+a/(
u\sqrt{M}))=1+O(1/\sqrt{M})$; conclude $|\mathcal{H}_1(u)-\mathcal{H}_\infty(u)|\le Ce^{-cu}/\sqrt{M}$.

nodes.name: Bound $\Gamma'$-integral via Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 4.2 to obtain $\Re(f(z)-f(\pi_1))\le -c$ on $\Gamma'$, hence the $\Gamma'$-integral is $O(e^{-\epsilon u}e^{-cM})$, exponentially small.

nodes.name: Treat $\mathcal{J}$ via direct steep-descent
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal{J}$, no residue is needed since $z=\pi_1$ is the right critical point of $-f$; use Lemma 4.1 plus Gaussian Taylor expansion to obtain $|Z_M^{-1}\mathcal{J}(v)-\mathcal{J}_\infty(v)|\le Ce^{-cv}/\sqrt{M}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.4 (b)
nodes.statement: From Proposition 4.1, the kernel $\int_0^\infty \mathcal{H}_\infty(x+u+y)\mathcal{J}_\infty(x+v+y)\,dy$ rewrites, using Hermite generating function, forward shift formula and Rodrigues formula, as the kernel $\sqrt{k}\, e^{-\epsilon u}\frac{p_k(u)p_{k-1}(v)-p_{k-1}(u)p_k(v)}{u-v} e^{-v^2/2} e^{\epsilon v}$, whose Fredholm determinant equals $G_k$ via the orthogonal polynomial method.

nodes.name: Express $\mathcal{H}_\infty,\mathcal{J}_\infty$ via Hermite
nodes.statement: Use the Hermite generating function $\sum H_n(x)t^n/n!=e^{2xt-t^2}$ and Rodrigues formula to write $-ie^{\epsilon u}\mathcal{H}_\infty(u)=(-1)^{k-1}(2\pi)^{1/4}/\sqrt{k!}\cdot p_k'(u)$ and $e^{-\epsilon v}\mathcal{J}_\infty(v)=(-1)^k i (2\pi)^{-1/4}\sqrt{k!}\,e^{-v^2/2}p_k(v)$.

nodes.name: Use Hermite ODE to integrate the kernel
nodes.statement: Apply the Hermite ODE $p_k''(y)-yp_k'(y)+kp_k(y)=0$ inside the integral $\int_0^\infty (u+y)p_k'(u+y)p_k(v+y)e^{-(v+y)^2/2}\,dy$ and integrate by parts the $(v+y)e^{-(v+y)^2/2}$ factor.

nodes.name: Christoffel-Darboux form via forward-shift identity
nodes.statement: Use $p_k'(y)=\sqrt{k}p_{k-1}(y)$ to obtain $K_2(u,v)=\sqrt{k}e^{-\epsilon u}\frac{p_k(u)p_{k-1}(v)-p_{k-1}(u)p_k(v)}{u-v}e^{-v^2/2}e^{\epsilon v}$, the Christoffel-Darboux kernel of GUE; conjugation cancels the $e^{\pm\epsilon}$ factors and the determinant equals $G_k$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1.5 (finite-N case)
nodes.statement: Compute $\mathbb{P}(\lambda_1\le t)$ from the eigenvalue density (with $\pi_1=\dots=\pi_k$), substitute $y_j=(1+\xi_j/\sqrt{M})/\pi_1$, identify the Selberg normalization $(2\pi)^{k/2}\prod (1+j)!$, and apply dominated convergence to obtain $G_k$.

nodes.name: Last passage time equals largest sample eigenvalue
nodes.statement: If $X(i,j)$ are independent exponentials of mean $1/(M\pi_i)$, then for $M\ge N$, $\mathbb{P}(L(M,N)\le x)=\mathbb{P}(\lambda_1(M,N)\le x)$, where $\lambda_1$ is the largest eigenvalue of the complex Gaussian sample covariance matrix.
conclusions: $L(N,M)$ has the same distribution as $\lambda_1$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.1
nodes.statement: Specialize the geometric-LPP formula $\mathbb{P}(G(N,M)\le n)=\prod(1-x_iy_j)\sum_{\lambda:\lambda_1\le n} s_\lambda(x)s_\lambda(y)$ from RSK with parameters $x_i=1-M\pi_i/L,y_j=1$ and let $L\to\infty$; the sum converges to the eigenvalue density (Equation 2.1).

nodes.name: Heuristic explanation of critical value $1+\gamma^{-1}$
nodes.statement: Conditioning the LPP path to follow the first column up to $(1,xM)$ and then enter the bulk gives leading-order last-passage time $f(x)=\pi_1^{-1}x+(\sqrt{1-x}+\gamma^{-1})^2$. The maximum over $x\in[0,1]$ jumps from $x=0$ (subcritical) to $x>0$ (supercritical) precisely when $\pi_1^{-1}>1+\gamma^{-1}$, matching the critical value of Theorem 1.4.

nodes.name: Queueing model equivalent
nodes.statement: The total exit time $E(M,N)$ for $M$ customers through $N$ tellers (service time at teller $i$ exponential of mean $1/(\pi_i M)$) satisfies the same recurrence $E(M,N)=\max\{E(M-1,N),E(M,N-1)\}+e(N)$ as $L(M,N)$, hence $E(M,N)\stackrel{d}{=}L(M,N)\stackrel{d}{=}\lambda_1$.
